title: Anonymous 'Ox Alpha' coding model tops DeepSWE, fingerprints point to Zhipu
subtitle: A free 1M-context model that appeared on OpenRouter and OpenCode last week is beating GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Fable 5 on early coding tests — and its Java stack traces name a Zhipu API path.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: An anonymous model listed as 'stealth/ox-alpha' appeared on OpenRouter and the OpenCode terminal agent on August 20 with a 1,048,576-token context window, text-image-video input, and a one-week free preview. By the weekend, community benchmarks put it at 80% on DeepSWE — ahead of Claude Fable 5 at 65% and GPT-5.6 Sol at 52% on the same 10-task suite. Claude Code was routing about 9.3 billion tokens per day through it by August 23, according to OpenRouter's own dashboard, making it the platform's top-consumed model despite carrying no lab attribution.

The reason SiliconANGLE and others took the story seriously is that a malformed request to OpenCode's Ox Alpha route returned a Java stack trace naming com.wd.paas.api.domain.v4.chat.ChatCompletionRequest — the exact path documented in Zhipu AI's /api/paas/v4/chat/completions endpoint. Independent fingerprinting layered on top: Ox Alpha's video encoder token usage matches GLM-5V-Turbo, its tokenizer aligns with GLM-5.3, it refuses audio input the same way Zhipu models do, and it drops emoji into replies at the same rate. No one at Zhipu has claimed it, and OpenRouter's stealth-model policy allows a lab to run a full public rollout before naming the model.

Ox Alpha lands into a month already crowded with open coding models — Meta's Muse Glimmer, Alibaba's Qwen3.8, and Zhipu's own GLM-5.3, held back for cyber-safety review after it surfaced 2,436 vulnerabilities in 269 open-source projects. If Ox Alpha is Zhipu's next step, it means the lab has moved from post-training tricks on GLM-5.3 to a full new frontier model — one that ships free, at 1M context, on infrastructure Anthropic's Claude Code is already routing production traffic to. The DeepSWE score is small-sample and the benchmark isn't audited, but the volume of routed tokens is not.

A note for learners: 'stealth' listings are a cheap way for a lab to buy a week of unfiltered production feedback before formally announcing a model. The signal is not the leaderboard number — it is whether professional users keep routing traffic to it after the free window closes. If Ox Alpha keeps its share once pricing appears, that tells you the benchmark held up under real workloads. If Claude Code and OpenCode users drop it the day the meter starts, the numbers were noise.
